item.title: Ambani’s Streaming Site Eyes Millions of Indian Diaspora
item.description: India’s largest video streaming platform JioHotstar is expanding overseas for the first time, launching in the UK, Canada and Singapore as it seeks to tap millions of potential viewers in the growing South Asian diaspora.

item.title: Asian Stocks Set for Declines as Oil Extends Gains: Markets Wrap
item.description: Asian stocks were set to decline Wednesday as surging oil prices pushed bond yields higher and stoked fears that resurgent inflation will force central banks to tighten monetary policy.

item.title: Latest Oil Market News and Analysis for Sept. 2
item.description: Oil advanced for a third session on heightened concerns about prolonged disruptions to energy flows through the Strait of Hormuz after an escalation of hostilities between the US and Iran.

item.title: Germany Plans Measures to Curb China Trade in Coming Weeks
item.description: Germany plans to agree on a package of measures in the coming weeks to counter what it sees as unfair Chinese trade practices, Finance Minister Lars Klingbeil said after visiting a BMW plant in Spartanburg, South Carolina.

item.title: Bessent’s Bond Gains Wiped Out as Treasury Yields Jump Again
item.description: The yields on the longest-dated US government bonds shot back to levels seen just before Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent shocked markets last month by expanding a buyback program in an effort to halt the rise.

item.title: Vanguard, BlackRock ETF Shuffle Lets Foreign Investors Duck US Tax
item.description: Major institutions are flipping between near-identical equity funds to avoid receiving dividends — and the 30% tax that comes with them.

item.title: Dropbox User Accounts Breached by Hackers Who Accessed Data
item.description: Hackers broke into thousands of Dropbox Inc. accounts last month, viewing and downloading material users kept on the cloud-storage platform, according to a company statement and records seen by Bloomberg News.

item.title: Apple Sets Pay Targets at $58 Million for Ternus, $47 Million for Cook
item.description: Apple Inc. said that new Chief Executive Officer John Ternus will get a compensation package worth about $58 million in fiscal 2027, while Tim Cook’s role as executive chairman will pay around $47 million.

item.title: Nokia to Rejoin Euro Stoxx 50 Index as Volkswagen Loses Its Spot
item.description: Nokia Oyj is regaining its spot in the euro area’s main stock benchmark as Volkswagen AG loses its place in the latest sign of the difficulties facing the region’s automotive industry.

item.title: Canadian Stocks Erase a Month of Gain as Tech, Banks, Gold Slide
item.description: Canadian stocks suffered their worst rout in nearly a month as an escalation in tensions in the Middle East added to worries about inflation and sparked a selloff in shares of high-flying technology and financial companies.

item.title: Canada Can Ride Out Global Bond Rout, Finance Minister Says
item.description: Finance Minister Francois-Philippe Champagne said positive investor sentiment is helping keep Canada’s borrowing costs in check despite a global bond rout, arguing the country’s finances are strong enough to handle the volatility.

item.title: Palo Alto Networks Tops Profit Outlook on AI Security Demand
item.description: The cybersecurity firm Palo Alto Networks Inc. issued a profit outlook for the year that exceeded Wall Street’s expectations, fueled by corporate demand for stronger defenses against advancing artificial intelligence systems.

item.title: Apple Maps Renames Lake Ontario ‘Lake America’ After Trump Order
item.description: Apple Inc. renamed Lake Ontario “Lake America” on its maps service, following a similar move by Alphabet Inc.’s Google, in the wake of an order from US President Donald Trump.

item.title: Dell Gains After Surging AI Server Sales Spur Boost in Outlook
item.description: Dell Technologies Inc. shares jumped in extended trading after the company boosted its annual sales forecast by $25 billion in a further sign of surging demand for servers to run artificial intelligence tasks.

item.title: OpenAI Will Limit Access to New Astra Model’s Cybersecurity Features
item.description: OpenAI plans to soon roll out a powerful new artificial intelligence model called Astra, but said it will limit who can use the software’s most cutting-edge cybersecurity capabilities.

item.title: New Leaks Draw Brazil Top Court Judge Deeper Into Banco Master Scandal
item.description: A prominent Brazilian Supreme Court judge is facing renewed scrutiny over alleged ties to Banco Master SA after the release of text messages from the former owner of the failed lender.

item.title: Florida Bans Flock Cameras, License Plate Readers From State Roads
item.description: Florida banned local police from installing license-plate readers on state roads, responding to growing concern about the proliferation of surveillance cameras made by Flock Safety and other companies.

item.title: Bond Traders Snap Up Protection Against Soaring Treasury Yields
item.description: Traders are scrambling to shield their portfolios against further losses in Treasuries, as worries over the budget deficit and inflation push yields toward multiyear highs.

item.title: Republicans Seek More Changes at Hobbled Consumer Watchdog
item.description: A group of House Republicans unveiled a proposal that aims to overhaul the structure of the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau, which has been entangled in legal fights as the Trump administration moves to cut the agency’s funding and staffing.

item.title: European Gas Prices Hit Highest Since 2023 as Iran War Escalates
item.description: European natural gas prices surged to their highest since January 2023 after an escalation of hostilities in the US-Iran war amplified worries about a prolonged disruption to Middle East energy.

item.title: Bitcoin ETF Buyers Return as $80,000 Level Tests Market Rally
item.description: The investors who helped propel Bitcoin into its Wall Street era are showing signs of coming back, offering a crucial test of whether its latest rally can turn into something bigger.

item.title: SEC Preps Plan to Widen Investor Access to Private Markets
item.description: The US Securities and Exchange Commission is eyeing a plan to expand access for retail investors to private markets and allow investment advisers to charge performance fees to a wider set of clients.

item.title: JPMorgan’s Aliaga Says Market Can Absorb ‘Attractive’ Tech Debt
item.description: JPMorgan Asset Management’s Stephanie Aliaga said that the bond market can absorb the growing supply of hyperscaler debt, as rising artificial intelligence demand reassures investors that the companies can pay their obligations.

item.title: Finland Narrows Deficit in 2027 Budget as Economy Recovers
item.description: Finland’s government agreed on a budget for next year that supports economic recovery while Prime Minister Petteri Orpo’s four-party coalition tries to rein in public debt growth.

item.title: Why Government Bond Yields Are Rising and Causing Alarm
item.description: Government borrowing costs have been surging around the world as investors demand more compensation to entice them to hold longer-maturity debt. Yields on 30-year Japanese government bonds are near all-time highs at 4.19%, while 30-year UK government bond yields are at their highest since 1998. A Bloomberg gauge tracking government debt across the Group of Seven countries now yields its highest on average since September 2000.

item.title: Nestle Sells Vitamins Business to Private Equity for $1 Billion
item.description: Nestle SA plans to sell its mainstream vitamins and supplements business to US private equity firm Yellow Wood Partners for $1 billion as Chief Executive Officer Philipp Navratil tries to streamline and turn around the Swiss foodmaker.

item.title: Apple Ternus Touts Product Pipeline, ‘Phenomenal’ Sept. 9 iPhone Launch in Memo
item.description: Apple Inc. Chief Executive Officer John Ternus touted the company’s strong product pipeline and teased a “phenomenal” iPhone launch next week in his first remarks to employees as their new leader.

item.title: Bessent Suggests Backing for BOJ Action in Meeting With Ueda
item.description: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent, who’s repeatedly signaled that Japan needs higher interest rates to bolster the yen, suggested he’s supporting such a move after a meeting with Bank of Japan Governor Kazuo Ueda.

item.title: Apple’s Former CFO Maestri Drops Role Running Corporate Services
item.description: With John Ternus beginning his role as Apple Inc. chief executive officer this week, another mainstay from the Tim Cook era is dropping his late-career responsibilities.

item.title: Bond Market Selloff: Are Surging Yields a Threat to the Global Stock Rally?
item.description: In equity markets, the myth goes that the only way is up. That perception has gained traction as global stock prices have largely ignored the selloff in bond markets. Yields on long-dated government debt have surged to near two-decade highs as investors worry about whether inflation and fiscal deficits can be tamed, and as sovereign bonds compete with an AI-fueled corporate borrowing boom.
